feedback.problem: Determine the points where the ellipse ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-2x-12y+35=0$ intercepts the $y$-axis.
feedback.worked_solution:
To calculate the $y$-intercepts, we need to substitute $x=0$ in the equation of the ellipse and try to solve the resulting equation for $y.$ We do this and solve the resulting equation by completing the square:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-2x-12y+35 & =0 \\ {0}^{2}+{y}^{2}-2(0)-12y+35 & =0 \\ {y}^{2}-12y+35 & =0 \\ (y-6)^{2}-36+35 & =0 \\ (y-6)^{2} & =1 \\ y-6 & =\pm 1 \\ y & =6\pm 1 \\ y & =5,\,7\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the ellipse intercepts the $y$-axis at $(0,5)$ and $(0,7).$
